text:
Carolina was the better team for most of this game and still lost by three. The Hurricanes finished with 3.97 expected goals to Washington's 3.08 and 81 shot attempts to 43, and the numbers say they deserved to win 64 percent of the time. But Washington scored three times in the first period, and Alex Tuch got two of them, including a backhand on a 54 percent chance that made it 3-0 at 14:23. That one swung the night.

The Capitals led that first period 2.17 to 0.71 in expected goals, then watched Carolina flip it in the second, 2.40 to 0.58. Jakob Chychrun stretched the lead to 4-0 early in that period with a power-play snap shot on a 3 percent chance, the least likely goal of the game. Sebastian Aho got one back on the power play at 16:50, and Ryan Leonard answered eight seconds later to make it 5-1. Logan Thompson did the rest, stopping 31 of 33 shots and saving 1.97 goals more than the chances he faced were worth. That included a 25 percent look for Jordan Martinook in the first.

Brandon Bussi stopped 22 of 27 and finished 1.92 goals below expectation, though Washington's even-strength expected goals (2.92 to 1.85) show the Capitals were sharp when it counted. Carolina went 1 for 6 on the power play despite 2.09 expected goals there. Logan Stankoven tipped in a goal in the third to make it 5-2, and that was all the Hurricanes got. Thompson was named the second star, behind Tuch.
